frequency_question: How often do structural frictions in tech transfer and high-tech manufacturing prevent the successful operational establishment of a complex weapons production line within a compressed timeline?
membership_rule: Includes state-level programs where an external advanced missile design is transferred to a recipient state for domestic assembly or manufacturing during an active conflict or severe crisis, excluding purely indigenous designs or simple non-guided munitions.
window: 1970 to present, covering modern missile technology transfers.

cases.name: Taiwan Hsiung Feng III domestic missile production setup (1990s)
Iran Soumar/Quds cruise missile reverse-engineering and production (2010s)
India BrahMos localization and second-site production initiatives (2010s-2020s)

coverage_note: 4 named cases representing major modern missile technology localization efforts under constraints; data is sparse due to classification.
known_gaps: Classified bilateral defense agreements between Western powers and allies regarding missile tech sharing are largely undocumented in open sources.
skeleton: Recipients attempting rapid transfer of Western-standard complex cruise missile manufacturing vs. those attempting indigenous or non-Western adaptations.
multiplier: 3 hits out of 4 documented major attempts at establishing localized cruise missile production lines under duress or external assistance.
validity_reason: Manufacturing technology and geopolitical controls on missile technology remain relatively stable over a 5-year horizon.
